top_stories.title: SpaceXAI Releases Grok 4.7 Coding Model
points: New flagship coding/knowledge model priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens (or up to $12 for a faster variant), with no price increase over prior version.
Nearly doubles coding performance on Terminal-Bench (a benchmark testing AI coding ability in real terminal environments) to 38.0%, and scores 19.6% on legal benchmarks.

Built on a larger base model with longer reinforcement training (extra training that rewards correct outputs to improve quality), can self-verify outputs, and handles agentic tasks (multi-step workflows where AI autonomously makes decisions and takes actions) via Grok Build.
Available across multiple platforms including Cursor, APIs, and cloud services.

top_stories.title: Xiaomi Launches Open-Source MiMo-V2.6-Pro and Flash AI Models
points: MiMo-V2.6-Pro and lighter Flash variant are MIT-licensed and available on Hugging Face for commercial use, targeting agent development teams.

Both support coding, tool use, multimodal input (text, images, and audio together), and a 1-million-token context window (the amount of text an AI can process at once, here equal to about 750,000 words).
MiMo-V2.6-Pro scored 46 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, the highest among openly available models, priced at $0.44 per million input tokens and $0.87 per million output tokens.

Uses a mixture-of-experts design (a technique where only relevant portions of a large neural network activate per task) with 1.02 trillion total parameters but only 42 billion active per request, cutting compute costs.
Xiaomi achieved this performance jump via reinforcement learning in under 6 days for about $2.62 million.
Flash delivers much of Pro's agent performance at a fraction of the cost, appealing to teams running large volumes of agent calls.

items.title: Google's Googlebooks: Premium Android Laptops Enter Market
points: Googlebooks launch October 4 starting at $899, with five models available for preorder; only one model is priced under $1,000, positioning them as premium devices versus budget Chromebooks.
Core differentiators are premium hardware, on-device apps, and powerful development tools, with Gemini AI models deeply integrated into the software.
Marks Google's pivot from the low-cost laptop category toward high-end computing with a productivity focus.

items.title: Google Defeats Supply-Chain Hacking Group from Inside
points: TeamPCP, a hacking gang, tainted hundreds of open-source programs with malware and breached 1,000+ companies through stolen developer accounts.
An undercover Google security analyst infiltrated TeamPCP during peak operations, letting Google monitor attacks in real time and warn targeted companies.
The group used a Dune-themed worm to automate exploitation; Google's infiltration disrupted their campaigns.

items.title: AI Model Landscape: New Categories and Pricing Models
points: Jev introduces 'System One' or 'Decision Models,' a new LLM category that accepts text input but outputs only numerical classifications, confidence scores, or yes/no answers, with free output pricing and $0.042 per million input tokens.
Meta's Muse mobile app outpaced ChatGPT's early adoption, with more downloads in its first 12 days in the US/Canada than ChatGPT achieved in its debut 12 days.

items.title: Robotics and Space: Market Constraints Reshape Industry Timeline
points: Agility Robotics went public at a $2.5 billion valuation; its Digit v5 robot launches later this year, able to work alongside humans instead of isolated in cages, with fast charging and swappable end effectors.
Rocket supply crunch: SpaceX is ending Falcon 9 rideshare missions to focus on Starship, with launch demand expected to exceed supply through the end of the decade and prices rising.
Multiple rockets under development are behind schedule, creating a market imbalance that favors existing launch providers.

items.title: Hermes Plugin Bridges Claude Subscription and Agent Frameworks
points: Claude Subscription DirectSDK lets the Hermes agent tap existing Claude Pro or Max allowances without a separate API key or pay-per-use billing.
The plugin runs the actual Claude app in the background, consuming allowance roughly 1.7x faster than using Claude Code directly.
Reduces friction for teams wanting advanced agents without managing separate billing.

items.title: Senior Engineer Career Trap: The 'Death Spiral'
points: Promotion trap: engineers grab the biggest project, disappear into work, and slowly fall behind on communication and visibility.
Risk is amplified by remote work and coding agents, which hide problems through less casual contact, more individual ownership, and fewer obvious warning signs.
Escape route: drop complexity, take on grunt work, build momentum through small daily wins, and share progress loudly so silence doesn't read as trouble.
Recovery depends on reputation built through shipping and communication, not just code quality.

items.title: OpenAI's Math Problem Milestone & Oversight
points: OpenAI's internal model solved 100+ previously unsolved math problems across multiple fields, beyond the disputed Navier-Stokes work.
An independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI was formed at Princeton with 9 mathematicians to oversee how results are assessed and announced.
The panel is unpaid and advisory-only, unable to steer research pace or halt projects.
Founding member Camillo De Lellis signed a warning letter stating that competition between AI companies pressures the math community, raising concerns about incentive structures.

items.title: Meta Patches Muse AI Agent Security Flaw
points: A zero-day vulnerability (a previously unknown security gap) in Muse for macOS let local attackers hijack the AI agent's account by rerouting cloud dictation to a malicious server.
Attackers could abuse the agent's permissions to take photos and write harmful files, often without user notification.
Meta patched the flaw within hours of public disclosure, but security researcher Patrick Wardle criticized the company for not building security in from the start.
Meta downplayed the risk as a 'local attack' requiring malicious code already on the machine, a characterization Wardle disputed.

items.title: Alibaba's Zhenwu V900 AI Chip & Expansion
points: Alibaba unveiled the Zhenwu V900 accelerator, claimed as China's most powerful AI chip, reportedly 3x faster than the previous version and able to run in clusters of up to 500,000 units.
The company plans to build a training system for models with 5-10 trillion parameters, far larger than current open-weight rivals.
Alibaba's chip unit T-Head, planned for public listing, has shipped 560,000 units of the Zhenwu family to over 400 customers.
Alibaba is backing the AI push with over $53 billion in investment over three years.

items.title: Apple Opens Music Hall in London
points: Apple opened Music Hall, a 600-seat live venue in London featuring spatial audio recording and broadcast-quality production capabilities.
